+# Working notes — programmes fed by card V3 (computed capsid–receptor binding calls)
+
+Card: V3 "Motif calls emitted for Capsida NR001–NR005 and Lir Starfish binding-assay readouts".
+Root question: which AAV variants transcytose the BBB vs stay intracellular, for which capsid–receptor binding signatures.
+Card's step: computed bind/no-bind calls (docking + AlphaFold-Multimer seeds + MD) for 36 capsid–receptor pairs (ALPL, AAVR, LRP6 panel), scored on published labels with threefold-axis interface geometry; compute lever 54→432 runs.
+Predicted outcomes: if_lever = balanced accuracy 0.80 at 432 runs vs 0.55 at 54, 5/6 binders within 5 Å of published sites; if_not = accuracy moves <0.05, ≤3/6 binders reach sites.
+
+## Programme picks (1–3)
+
+1. **Capsida Biotherapeutics** — the option explicitly frames the output format as their NR001–NR005 plate- and bead-based receptor binding assays. Consumer of computed calls as a pre-filter for their wet-lab binding step.
+2. **Lir Therapeutics (Starfish™ / nAAVigator®)** — the option explicitly names "Lir's Starfish capsid-structure pipeline"; their docking-at-symmetry-axes step is exactly what the card scores.
+3. **CLOVER Center / Gradinaru Laboratory, Caltech (APPRAISE)** — the closest prior programme (Shay et al. 2024 is the card's closest_prior) and the publisher of APPRAISE, the open-source binding-propensity tool. Note: Gradinaru is co-founder/BoD member of Capsida (CaltechAUTHORS conflict statement), so picks 1 and 3 are linked.
+
+## Evidence per programme
+
+### 1. Capsida Biotherapeutics (capsida.com)
+- Step (own words, conference deck PDF): slide "In Vitro Binding Platform Demonstrates Reproducible Capsid/Receptor Binding Data Consistent with Expression Profiles" with "Plate-Based Receptor Binding Detection" / "Bead-Based Receptor Binding Detection"; sentence used as step_quote: "The predictive power of in vitro receptor binding is confirmed by AAV transduction in cell lines with receptor expression" (deck URL: https://capsida.com/wp-content/uploads/Nick_Goeden_1445_May-14_Theater-C_Identification-of-Multiple-BBB-Receptors.pdf). Deck text extracted via search index of the PDF (PDF is binary on direct fetch; quotes match the extracted text layer).
+- Deck also: "Capsida Biotherapeutics has successfully filed patents for all five of these groundbreaking novel receptors and is focused on further expanding the IP portfolio surrounding them" (NR001–NR005 receptors proprietary — supports gap).
+- Scale/tools (science-innovation page): "At Capsida, the scale at which we have engineered capsids is unrivaled. Using our automated, high-throughput biological screening, our scientists assess large, diverse engineered capsid libraries for CNS and the eye in models relevant to humans to quickly identify optimal capsids that target tissues and cells in organs of interest." https://capsida.com/science-innovation/
+- Also: "We have identified novel human blood-brain barrier receptors that bind our engineered capsids and are conserved between primates and humans." (same page)
+- Activity: May 12, 2026 press release (ASGCT 2026 abstracts 2031/3233, CSO Romuald Corbau appointed, CNS update). https://capsida.com/capsida-to-present-preclinical-data-of-new-next-generation-high-performing-ocular-capsids-at-asgct-annual-meeting/ — quote: "Capsida Biotherapeutics, ("Capsida") a next-generation genetic medicines company, today provided corporate and pipeline updates related to its ocular and central nervous system (CNS) programs." Also on that page: "The ongoing experiments include studying the interaction between the engineered viral capsid contained in CAP-002 and the ADAM15 protein, its primary receptor for crossing the blood brain barrier (BBB). Based on the learning over the past six months, Capsida believes that the receptor is a key factor in designing CNS gene therapy." and "we are making progress with a new capsid that uses a distinct receptor, RECK, to cross the blood-brain barrier". State: active.
+- Pipeline page (capsida.com/pipeline) listing: "May 12, 2026 Capsida to Present Preclinical Data..." and "May 11, 2026 CAP-002 Program Update: A Letter to the STXBP1 Community".
+- already_done: unknown — public materials show experimental binding detection and receptor-interaction investigations (ADAM15, RECK); no public record of exhaustive computed pose enumeration scored against their plate/bead labels; assays/receptors proprietary.
+
+### 2. Lir Therapeutics (lirtx.com)
+- Step (Starfish post): "Starfish™ rapidly identifies relevant binding surfaces for capsid multimers using cost-efficient hardware, enabling Lir to incorporate essential capsid structural analysis into large-scale viral variant library screenings." https://www.lirtx.com/post/starfish-fast-capsid-structure-generation
+- Threefold-axis sentence (step_quote candidate): "Owing to its structural homogeneity, modelling the complete 60-mer AAV capsid is usually unnecessary, but portions of the surface such as at the 2, 3 and 5-fold axes are the minimum subunit for useful docking or structural assessment of capsid stability in silico."
+- Applications (their binding-call use): "We first showcased an application of this technology at ESGCT 2025 in Seville, demonstrating that screening of the LY6A receptor was possible by performing docking to variant capsid surfaces constructed using Starfish™. We found a structural approach identified an alternative subset of hits compared to a language model-based approach, with the two methods being additive." Also "We've been using this same approach for other receptors to investigate experimental targets predicted to exhibit differential binding." and "We've found larger docking surfaces have been required to get relevant docking scores for screening purposes. Starfish is an important aspect of our work to both generate variants and add explainability to hits".
+- Scale: "Our method scales far better than multimer cofolding both in terms of runtime and compute requirements, with Starfish™ able to assemble the full capsid at acceptable runtimes for screening tens of thousands of variants." Benchmarks: "All approaches generate the 3-fold axes of AAV9 wild-type with an RMSD <1Å, but Starfish™ provides a clear advantage in runtime and scalability."
+- Activity: blog index (https://www.lirtx.com/blog) posts dated July 15, 2026 ("The immune system doesn't want your gene therapy to work"), June 17, 2026, May 1, 2026, Feb 4, 2026 (Starfish), Dec 18, 2025 (LirEvolve). Most recent partnership: VectorBuilder newsroom Aug 18, 2026 — "VectorBuilder, a global leader in gene delivery technologies, and Lir Therapeutics, a company pushing the boundaries of vector engineering with AI, today announced a strategic collaboration to develop adeno-associated virus (AAV) capsids designed not only for strong biological performance, but also for the manufacturability and scalability required to bring gene therapies into the clinic." http://en.vectorbuilder.com/about-us/newsroom.html (also pharmaSource Aug 19, 2026). State: active.
+- already_done: partly — LY6A docking screens on Starfish-built variant surfaces (ESGCT 2025) + other receptors; no published bind/no-bind accuracy vs a labelled grid, no 54→432 run scaling; their hits differ from language-model hits.
+
+### 3. CLOVER Center / Gradinaru Laboratory, Caltech (APPRAISE) — clover.caltech.edu, GradinaruLab/APPRAISE
+- Step quote (APPRAISE GitHub README): "Automated Pair-wise Peptide-Receptor binding model AnalysIs for Screening Engineered proteins (APPRAISE) is a method that predicts the receptor binding propensity of engineered proteins based on high-precision protein structure prediction tools, such as AlphaFold2-multimer." https://github.com/GradinaruLab/APPRAISE — 213 commits, PyPI package appraise (1.2.6), Colab notebook; README currently documents Boltz-1/Chai-1/OpenFold3 BETA backends.
+- Manuscript (Ding, Chen, Sullivan, Shay, Gradinaru, Molecular Therapy 2024), abstract at https://authors.library.caltech.edu/records/nyxge-gz849 : "After generating structural models of engineered proteins competing for binding to a target using an established structure prediction tool such as AlphaFold-Multimer or ESMFold, APPRAISE performs a rapid (under 1 CPU second per model) scoring analysis that takes into account biophysical and geometrical constraints." and "As proof-of-concept cases, we demonstrate that APPRAISE can accurately classify receptor-dependent vs. receptor-independent adeno-associated viral vectors and diverse classes of engineered proteins such as miniproteins targeting the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike, nanobodies targeting a G-protein-coupled receptor, and peptides that specifically bind to transferrin receptor or programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1)." Conflict statement: "V.G. is a scientific co-founder and BoD member of Capsida Biotherapeutics."
+- Closest prior (Shay et al. 2024, Nat Commun, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11381518/):
+  - Labels/scale of screen: "Here, we adapt an unbiased human cell microarray platform to determine the extracellular and cell surface interactomes of natural and engineered AAVs."; "we then tested the six-capsid pool in a full screen of over 6400 proteins, including 6019 human plasma membrane proteins and secreted and cell surface-tethered proteins, as well as 397 heterodimers."
+  - Modeling scale: "Representative AlphaFold models, from 5 structural models each of X1 and CAP-Mac peptides with up to 20 recycles, predict selective interaction with human LRP6 domain E1 (E1 and E2: teal, E3 and E4: yellow, AAV peptides: purple)."
+  - Tools: "The complex structures of the LRP6 extracellular domain and AAV-X1 or AAV.CAP-Mac VR-VIII peptide were modeled using a cloud-based implementation of AlphaFold-Multimer-v3 provided in ColabFold v2.3.5." + "We ran the Google Colaboratory notebook using an A100 SXM4 40GB GPU. Five structure models were produced using a protocol with up to 20 recycles..."
+  - Threefold geometry: "using a combination of biophysical techniques including cryo-ET sub-tomogram averaging with symmetry expansion, we were able to locate the human IL3 binding site on the side of AAV9's threefold symmetry spike adjacent to the capsid's twofold symmetry valley and generate an integrative binding model."
+  - SPR labels: "Both AAV9-X1.1 and CAP-Mac strongly bind human LRP6-Fc, unlike their parent capsid, AAV9, with a sub-nM apparent affinity."; "SPR of mouse LRP6-E1E2 and LRP6-E3E4 ... confirms that AAV9-X1.1 and CAP-Mac bind only to LRP6-E1E2."
+- Activity: CLOVER news Aug 27, 2026 "Chemical BBB shuttle targets CA-IV for potent brain delivery" (Nature Chemical Biology) — https://clover.caltech.edu/news/chemical-bbb-shuttle-targets-ca-iv-to-deliver-conjugated-payloads-to-the-brain : "Former CLOVER Research Scientists and Gradinaru lab alumns Xiaozhe Ding and Xinhong Chen led a multidisciplinary effort with fellow co-first authors from the Reisman lab at Caltech that generated a small molecule shuttle to efficiently deliver biological cargo across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) of mice and non-human primates." Also March 30, 2026 "Structural basis of AAV liver de-targeting and neuronal tropism" (Molecular Therapy) — "CLOVER-affiliated graduate student Tyler Brittain and Postdoctoral Fellow Seongmin Jang led a team effort to determine the structural basis of AAV tropism modulation away from liver and non-neuronal CNS cells using cryo-EM, biophysical assays, and in vivo characterization of CAP-B10, AAV9-X1.1, and other capsids." https://clover.caltech.edu/news/structural-basis-of-aav-liver-de-targeting-and-neuronal-tropism . State: active.
+- already_done: partly — APPRAISE proof-of-concept classifies receptor-dependent vs receptor-independent AAVs from computed models; Shay 2024 checked 5-model AF-Multimer LRP6-domain predictions against SPR E1E2/E3E4 labels and cryo-ET sites for ~6 capsids. No 36-pair grid at 54–432 runs with balanced-accuracy scoring and site-recovery counts.
+
+## Effect of the two outcomes (draft)
+- Capsida if_lever: in silico bind/no-bind gate ahead of plate/bead assays; threefold-site recovery becomes interface QC; hundreds of runs budgeted as validation for patented receptor panel. if_not: no change — wet-lab binding detection remains the gate; computed calls stay hypothesis-generating.
+- Lir if_lever: docking promoted from ranking heuristic to validated bind/no-bind call at the threefold patch; hundreds of pose/seed/MD runs budgeted in nAAVigator; no-bind pairs dropped before lab-in-the-loop. if_not: docking stays a ranking signal ("additive" with language models); surface-size tuning remains the only knob; extra pose sampling not justified.
+- CLOVER if_lever: APPRAISE/AF-Multimer scaled from 5–10 models per competition to hundreds of runs per pair; balanced-accuracy gating before SPR/cryo-ET; threefold-site tolerance becomes standard interface criterion. if_not: models stay illustrative; calls continue to come from SPR/pull-down/cryo-ET; APPRAISE remains rank-order hints with known false negatives.
+
+## Gaps
+- Public labels cover 13/36 pairs (card); Capsida NR001–NR005 receptor identities and assay labels are proprietary/patented — full grid can't be scored on Capsida's own labels.
+- No programme has published a 54→432 run-count scaling curve for binding-call accuracy; the lever question is open for all three.
+- Lir's docking benchmarks are blog/poster material (ESGCT 2025), not a peer-reviewed accuracy dataset; call accuracy not externally checkable.
+- Card yields binding-call agreement and interface geometry only; all three decide ultimately on transduction/transcytosis/in vivo data.
+- Capsida's current priority receptors (ADAM15, RECK) are outside the card's reference labels and public interface structures.
+
+## Fetch problems / caveats
+- Capsida deck PDF returns binary; quotes taken from the PDF text layer via search-index extraction of the same URL; cross-checked against the seed record's identical quotes (s_capsida_deck).
+- VectorBuilder PR page JS-heavy; quotes taken from the newsroom index page which carries the release text.

"Here is a research card, written to answer this root question: Can molecular mapping of AAV capsid-receptor interactions on brain microvascular endothelial cells determine which AAV variants transcytose across the blood-brain barrier versus remain intracellular, and for which capsid-receptor binding signatures?

**V3 · Motif calls emitted for Capsida NR001–NR005 and Lir Starfish binding-assay readouts.** seed pick · compute tested: yes · plan expects: not the lever · PASS

**Question.** Can computed capsid–receptor binding calls for ALPL, AAVR and LRP6 reproduce published bind/no-bind readouts with interfaces at the threefold axis?

**What is known.** Shay and colleagues in 2024 ran five AlphaFold-Multimer models per peptide and used cryo-ET to map where LRP6 and IL3 bind engineered capsids, with SPR binding labels [s_shay_af]. Whether hundreds of pose and seed runs improve bind/no-bind agreement with threefold-axis geometry across a full capsid-by-receptor grid remains untested [s_shay_af].

**Hypothesis.** Pairs that bind in plate- and bead-based assays share threefold-axis or insert-loop engagement geometry, so pose enumeration recovers published bind/no-bind labels [s_aavr_struct].

**If compute is the lever.** Balanced accuracy 0.80 at 432 runs versus 0.55 at 54, with five of six known binders within 5 Å of published sites.

**If not.** Accuracy moves under 0.05 between 54 and 432 runs and at most three of six binders reach published sites; extra runs resample the wrong basin.

**Test.** Thirty-six capsid–receptor pairs run docking, three AlphaFold-Multimer seeds, two 5-ns MD relaxations; calls and threefold-site geometry scored on published labels; parallel wall-clock versus serial one-GPU and independent-copy baselines.

*Compute axis.* Independent capsid–receptor model runs (docking, AlphaFold-Multimer, MD relaxation) the answer needs: 54–432 model runs, 3 levels. Closest prior: 10 [s_shay_af], beyond it.

*Restructuring.* none.

**Check first.** Redocking AAVR-PKD2 onto AAV2 must place it beside the threefold spike matching PDB 6IHB contacts; serial and parallel pilots must match calls. Tolerance: >=50% contact overlap at the published 4.5 Å cutoff or interface backbone RMSD <=5 Å; serial versus parallel top-pose RMSD <=2 Å with identical bind/no-bind calls.

**Would not show.** Binding-call agreement and interface geometry only; no transcytosis or affinity. Public labels cover 13 of 36 pairs; NR001–NR005 and Starfish assays are proprietary.

*Cost.* Plans $506.83 of the $1,000 budget over 40 machine-hours, leaving $493.17. Main guess: GROMACS throughput on one A100 [p], measured after $107.46 of spend; the budget is reached if it is 4.5× lower.
